skill.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skill.description: Helps an AI assistant finish a completed development branch by verifying tests, offering merge or pull request choices, and cleaning up safely.
skill.summary: Finish completed development branches with test checks, merge choices, pull requests, and guarded cleanup.
skill.author: obra

security_audit.summary: The static command findings are mostly Markdown fence false positives, not executable Ruby or JavaScript patterns. The skill still carries operational risk because it guides git push, branch deletion, and worktree removal workflows. No prompt injection, credential access, or secret exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Show the exact branch, commits, and worktree path before deletion. Prefer non-force deletion when possible and keep the typed discard confirmation.
Confirm the remote, base branch, branch name, and pull request title before pushing. Do not publish if tests have not passed.

remediation.issue: Unquoted branch name in worktree check
remediation.suggestion: Quote the current branch value and use fixed-string matching when checking worktree output. This avoids option parsing and pattern matching surprises.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Git Cleanup Commands
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes branch deletion and worktree removal commands after a discard or cleanup flow. These commands can remove local work if the branch, base, or path is wrong, although the skill requires typed discard confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 116 through 147 explicitly describe typed discard confirmation followed by git branch deletion and worktree removal. The safeguards lower the risk, but the data loss impact is real.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Publication Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the assistant to push a feature branch and create a pull request. This can publish local work to the configured remote if consent or target repository details are misunderstood.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 89 through 104 contain the push and pull request workflow. The action is user-selected, so the concern is contextual rather than malicious.

content.value_statement: Finishing a branch can create confusion about tests, merge targets, and cleanup. This skill gives Claude, Codex, or Claude Code a clear workflow for final branch decisions.
actual_capabilities: Requires test verification before merge, pull request, or cleanup decisions.
Determines a likely base branch with git merge-base checks.
Presents four completion choices: merge locally, create a pull request, keep the branch, or discard work.
Runs the selected git workflow and repeats tests after a local merge.
Requires typed confirmation before discard and scopes worktree cleanup to selected options.
limitations: Requires the assistant to know or infer the correct project test command.
Does not resolve merge conflicts automatically.
Uses GitHub CLI for pull request creation when that option is selected.
Can remove local branches or worktrees if the user confirms discard.

use_cases.title: Complete a Feature Branch
use_cases.description: A developer has finished implementation and wants a structured final decision before merging or opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Handoffs
use_cases.description: A team lead wants assistants to use the same completion checklist for branch status, tests, and cleanup.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Worktree Tasks
use_cases.description: A repository maintainer wants worktrees and temporary branches handled only after tests and explicit user choice.

prompt_templates.title: Finish My Branch
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow after implementation is done.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to finish my current development branch. Verify tests first, then show me the completion options.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the branch finishing workflow. If tests pass, help me push this branch and create a clear pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Merge Locally After Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Finish this development branch. Verify tests, identify the base branch, and guide a local merge if I choose it.

prompt_templates.title: Finalize a Worktree Branch
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with branch cleanup risk.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the full branch finishing process for this worktree. Preserve work unless I explicitly choose cleanup or discard.

output_examples.input: Implementation is complete and tests pass.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports completion and asks whether to merge locally, create a pull request, keep the branch, or discard the work.

output_examples.input: The user chooses to create a pull request.
output_examples.output: The assistant pushes the branch only after confirmation, prepares a concise summary, and leaves the worktree preserved.

output_examples.input: The user asks to discard the branch.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists the branch, commits, and worktree path, then waits for the exact typed confirmation before deletion.

best_practices: Run the project test suite before offering completion choices.
Confirm the base branch and remote target before merge or pull request actions.
Use typed confirmation before any discard or deletion step.
anti_patterns: Do not merge or publish a branch with failing tests.
Do not delete a branch or worktree from an implied yes response.
Do not force-push or rewrite remote history as part of this workflow.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after implementation is complete and you need a final branch decision.

faq.question: Does it run tests before merge decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requires test verification before presenting completion options.

faq.question: Can it create a pull request?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide a push and pull request through GitHub CLI when selected.

faq.question: Can it discard work?
faq.answer: Yes, but only after showing what will be deleted and receiving typed confirmation.

faq.question: Does it clean up worktrees automatically?
faq.answer: It cleans up worktrees only for selected flows where cleanup is part of the chosen outcome.

faq.question: Does it choose the base branch by itself?
faq.answer: It checks common base branches and can ask the user to confirm the correct base.
